paragraphs.text: Rabiah is a collection of one thousand and one originally identical planes , all refracted off of the original Rabiah during the Thousandfold Refraction . It is for this reason that Rabiah is known as "the Infinite". Over the centuries, these planes have since developed independently of each other. However, there are some general features that are consistent across almost all variations of Rabiah.

Rabiah is a desert world. Where Rabiah's touches another plane, the severe environment often begins to "infect" its neighbor. However, that rarely worries Rabiah's inhabitants, since they are hardy desert dwellers. Planar links in Rabiah often appear in the form of giant desert twisters. Such dust storms violently propel any who venture too near them into the particular plane the gates link to. One plane often linked to Rabiah is Wildfire ; another one is Dominaria , in particular the continent of Jamuraa .

Although most Rabian cultures are patriarchal and Arabic in feel, the vast range of Rabiahs also includes matriarchy. Furthermore, one plane, known as Dark Rabiah , has been taken over by sinister forces and is as evil a place as even Phyrexia .
Rabiah was the setting for the Arabian Nights expansion, and was based upon the One Thousand and One Nights collection of stories.

Baghdad Bazaar of Baghdad - the largest bazaar in Rabiah
Bassorah - a city inhabited by Bird Maidens , Desert Nomads and Gypsies Bazaar of Bassorah - the second largest bazaar in Rabiah Mosque Quarter of Bassorah - an area of temples and mosques.
Cairo - where Ali is from.
City of Brass - a city in the far reaches of Rabiah which reflects the sunlight, burning unwary visitors

Crags of Jaruq - a plateau of rough crags and cliffs, overlooking the Castle of El-Hajjâj . Castle of El-Hajjâj - a wizard 's citadel half-hidden behind an illusion City in a Bottle - a tiny city contained within a lamp
Crags of Sana'a - a mountainous region Nailah's Keep - fortress of the Sorceress Queen Nailah , formerly known as Castle of El-Hajjâj .
Fa'adiyah (fah-ah-DEE-ah ) - a forest, home to seers and to the Shepherd Taysir , who was killed there by the Apprentice Taysir at the Sorceress Queen Nailah 's command.
Island of Wak-Wak - home of winged people and strange, speaking fruit.
Karun Desert - a desert populated by nomads . This was where Nailah and the Apprentice Taysir found the Nomad, and where the duel between the Apprentice and Nailah took place.

Serendib (sair-en-DIHB ) is an island populated by vicious Djinn and Efreeti . It is named after the ancient name for Sri Lanka . In an alternate reality created by the Temporal Crisis of Dominaria there were human sorcerers from the island.
Sea of Sand - a sun-blased, interminable desert .

Mark Rosewater stated that Rabiah would likely never be revisited in a Standard-legal set, since it is not Wizards' own intellectual property. Continued prompting on this subject led him to create the Rabiah Scale , as a planar equivalent of the Storm Scale , on which Rabiah holds the highest (least likely) rank by definition. Even with the advent of the Universes Beyond creative treatment, Rosewater maintained that the plane as designed is not revisitable, but a mythology-inspired plane would have better odds. However, in September 2025 he finally wouldn't rule out that a new Middle Eastern inspired set would take place on Rabiah (provided it would receive a treatment like Neon Dynasty got for Kamigawa ). It even could be “the plane formerly known as Rabiah, now with a new name”.
